preview: Manav Abhang shares his JPMC interview and Code for Good hackathon experience, detailing the online coding test, video interview, hackathon rounds, and final internship offer.
content: Manav Abhang B.Tech CS INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE Registration Process: 10th March to 23rd March Online Coding Test: 7th April - 10th April Video Interview: Deadline 17th April Code for Good Shortlist announcement: 23th June Code for Good Event: 15th and 16th July Internship Shortlist announcement: 25th August Timeline LinkedIn 1) Maximum index a pointer can reach in N steps by avoiding a given index B (Link) => I could solve all the test case (14/14) and this one doesn’t require DSA but you can use STL (Very Imp Topic for DSA) and solve through Greedy Approach Online Coding Round (60 Minutes) This is the first step for SEP Selection Process Test were conducted on HackerRank and duration is 60 minutes. There were 2 Programming Question and the coding language can be C, C++, C#, Java 7, Java 8, Javascript, Python 2 & Python 3 2)Two Sums (Link) => I don’t remember second Question but it was relate to Two Sums. I wasn’t able to solve all the test case (12/14). Try to do 450DSA sheet which would help a lot in this kinds of problem 1) What are your achievements and what learning did you get from the same? 2) Talk about a recent experience where you learnt a lot. Video Interview (10 Minutes) This is the second step for SEP Selection Process Interview were conducted on HireVue and duration is 10 minutes. Test link were given on 15th April There were 2 Question asked and it was relate to HR Question , not coding question You have the opportunity to record your response again once for each question. If you choose to re-record any response, it will automatically be submitted as your final answer for that question. Practice Link After Coding Round and Video Interview, 15 students were selected for the CFG (Code for Good Hackathon) Before Hackathon: => Before the hackathon, a list came out with about seven people in each group, totaling around 550 individuals from different states, some from NIT or IIT, and others from local colleges. Then, we connected through LinkedIn and Slack. The most important platforms were Slack and Zoom, and there was one more thing (I can't recall, but it was for code submission; don't worry, they would explain how to download it before the hackathon started). => After the initial meeting, we created WhatsApp groups to get to know each other and find out about everyone's tech stack preferences, such as who does frontend or backend, API, or database work. => Later, we had a Zoom meeting where they explained the submission process and answered any doubts we had. We also received a list of mentors. Basically, we had three mentors, with only two conducting interviews, while the third observed the teams. We got to know the mentors, who were all very friendly. => After that, the problem statements were released. There were four in total, but we could only choose three. We discussed this among ourselves and with the mentors via WhatsApp and Zoom. The submission process for the problem statements was first in, first out (FIFO), so be ready to submit quickly, or you might end up with the second or third problem statement. Code for Good Hackathon This is the final step for SEP Selection Process Interview were conducted Online and duration is 24 hours. During Hackathon: =>During the hackathon, I served as a full-stack developer. Since my team lacked expertise in backend development, I and one other member took on the backend tasks while the rest focused on frontend work. We were deeply engaged in solving problems and interacting with mentors, which was crucial for our progress. We had extensive discussions about the backend challenges we encountered and sought guidance from mentors. There were two rounds of interviews, conducted one-on-one for each team member. The first round took place around 12:30 at night. The questions asked were: What tech stack have you learned? 1. Can you describe a project you've worked on, and about hackathons you've participated in? 2. Are you enjoying this hackathon? 3. Have you completed your tasks so far? (Even if you haven't completed them, don't worry, they won't be disappointed) 4. What subjects were you taught in college? 5. Only two questions were related to subjects: Explain joins and types of joins? (From DBMS) 1. Tell me about data structures and provide a real-life example (From DSA) 2. After the interviews, I continued working on the backend tasks, such as creating APIs and databases. All team members worked smoothly, although it took time to complete our tasks. Later, a second interview was conducted by another mentor around 5:30 in the morning. Similar questions were asked (as in the first round (1,2,3)), along with inquiries about any doubts we had and details about our college life and extracurricular activities. There were no questions about subjects in this round. We had three tasks to complete: creating a website, submitting our code on GitHub, and preparing a presentation and screen recording. We divided our work accordingly, and the submission deadline was 10 a.m. After Hackathon: =>Somehow, we managed to complete both the backend and frontend tasks, although not fully. We submitted our work and then took a break. Later, it was announced that presentations would begin at 11 a.m. We did our best and delivered our presentation, and the organizers were pleased with our solution. Following the presentations, the results were announced, and to our delight, we made it to the final round. We were incredibly excited about this. We gave our final presentation in the final round, but unfortunately, We didn't win the hackathon. => Despite not winning, we were still thrilled because we had enjoyed the hackathon immensely, and the mentors were excellent. It was a really positive experience getting to know others, learning about their tech stacks, and gaining new insights. Tips: Interaction with mentors and communication is the most important thing. 1. Even if you have only done frontend work, don't be afraid. It's not about the tech stack you used; it's about the solution you provide. 2. Focus on important subjects like DBMS and OS for interviews. 3. Regularly practice DSA questions (450Sheet or Striver Sheet) and make sure to attend hackathons (I used Coding Ninjas and LeetCode Platform). 4. Forget to mention that a Git Workshop was also conducted before the hackathon, where you learned about Git and GitHub. 5. Even if you didn't win, don't be disappointed because it's not about winning; it's about how well you participate in the hackathon. 6. Be confident, relaxed, and don't be shy. Also, avoid arguing with mentors. 7. Intership Offer: After 1 month, internship result were announced, 6 out of 10 received internship offers (from college), and all 6 accepted the offer since the results were announced From my Hackathon Team , 4 out of 7 received the offers.
